  If this is your first time, check out https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-requests-prs
  for our PR guidelines.
-->

## Problem

Counting the number of elements produced by an iterator currently requires converting it to a table and taking its length, which is less ergonomic.

## Solution

Add `vim.iter():count()`.

comment_data.body: Should explicitly mention here that it drains the iterator.

 end

comment_data.body: Needs a `--- @since 15`, but once that's added this looks good.

comment_data.body:
This part can be simplified, right?

```suggestion
  local count = math.abs(self._tail - self._head)
```
comment_data.diff_hunk:
@@ -1227,6 +1227,25 @@ function IterArray:enumerate()
   return self
 end
 
+--- Drains the iterator, counting the number of iterations and returning it.
+---
+--- @since 15
+--- @return integer
+function Iter:count()
+  return self:fold(0, function(acc)
+    return acc + 1
+  end)
+end
+
+--- @private
+--- @return integer
+function IterArray:count()
+  local inc = self._head < self._tail and 1 or -1
+  local count = (self._tail - self._head) * inc

comment_data.body: You're right, that's much simpler. Thanks 😊

comment_data.body:
missing coverage:

- `:rev():count()` (exercises the `math.abs` branch)
- `:filter(…):count()` verifies the fast path after `_tail` compaction
- after `:count()`, `:next()` is `nil` and a second `:count()` is `0`.
- Function iterator (`vim.iter(string.gmatch(...)):count()`)
- Empty = `0`.

comment_regular_data.body:
hmm, I think this was discussed somewhere either in PRs or issues (found it: #23233 ), please confirm

cc @gpanders
@gpanders I decided to add a separate implementation for array-backed iterators since it's straightforward.

need to update the types:

https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/d06bac614c2bc09db62e439b2e42ac7101653333/runtime/lua/vim/_meta.lua#L13

https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/d06bac614c2bc09db62e439b2e42ac7101653333/runtime/lua/vim/_meta.lua#L39

I would prefer `Iter:len()` , but I guess that implies constant-time performance so maybe `count()` is better?

@justinmk I generally expect iterators to provide a `count()` method, while `len()` is typically reserved for collections or already-materialized tables, where the length can be determined in constant time.

Ideally, we could provide an `IterArray:len()` method. However, I don't think it fits well with our current type system.
